entities.name: Asian subgroup heterogeneity
observations: U.S. data show substantial heterogeneity in cardiovascular risk factors across Asian immigrant subgroups; Indian-subcontinent immigrants had the highest overweight/obesity and diabetes prevalence, while Southeast Asian immigrants had the highest high-cholesterol prevalence.
The study recommends subgroup-disaggregated prevention and culturally informed care.

entities.name: Filipina diabetes mortality
observations: In 2018–2021, diabetes-related cardiovascular mortality among Asian-American females ranged from 10.8 per 100,000 in Japanese women to 19.9 per 100,000 in Filipina women.
Diabetes-related all-cause mortality ranged from 36.8 per 100,000 in Chinese women to 64.8 per 100,000 in Filipina women.

entities.name: South Asian ASCVD risk
observations: South Asians have higher proportional ASCVD mortality than other Asian groups and non-Hispanic White populations.
Common risks include diabetes, abdominal obesity, hypertension, insulin resistance, and healthcare or treatment barriers.

entities.name: Asian BMI risk thresholds
observations: Asian-American populations can have central adiposity and cardiometabolic risk at lower BMI than White populations.
Reviews support Asian-specific obesity thresholds commonly around BMI 25 or 27.5 rather than 30; Filipino-focused evidence reports adverse cardiovascular associations above approximately BMI 23–24.9.

entities.name: Asian pregnancy cardiometabolic risk
observations: Asian-American pregnancies had 12.3% gestational-diabetes prevalence overall, including 14.3% in Indian, 12.9% in Filipino, and 12.8% in Vietnamese women.
Risk varied by ancestry, with especially high predicted risk above BMI 23 in Japanese and Korean Americans; foreign-born mothers generally had higher predicted risk.

entities.name: Asian women smoking variation
observations: In 2018, smoking prevalence among Asian-American women ranged from 0.5% in Asian Indian-American women to 13.1% among Asian plus Pacific-Islander multiracial women.
Subgroup-specific tobacco assessment is preferable to assuming uniformly low smoking risk.

entities.name: Asian evidence gaps
observations: Cardiovascular outcomes vary greatly across Asian-American subgroups, but Chinese, Japanese, and Filipino groups are disproportionately studied while smaller groups are rarely represented.
Direct comparative treatment-outcome evidence for women across all subgroups remains limited.
